common.sentence: 先生、おはようございます。

language_specific.usage: A polite morning greeting; 先生 (せんせい) means teacher.

common.sentence: こんにちは、田中さん。

language_specific.pronunciation: The final は is pronounced わ in this greeting.
language_specific.usage: A daytime greeting; さん is a respectful suffix used after a name. 田中 is read たなか.

common.sentence: こんばんは、山田さん。

language_specific.pronunciation: The final は is pronounced わ in this greeting.
language_specific.usage: 山田 is read やまだ; さん is a respectful suffix used after a name.

common.sentence: おやすみなさい、またあした。

language_specific.usage: Said when parting for the night or before sleep.

common.sentence: ありがとう、たすかったよ。

language_specific.usage: A casual way to thank someone; たすかった means their help made a difference.

common.sentence: すみません、えきはどこですか。

language_specific.usage: Used here to get someone's attention politely before a question.

common.sentence: ごめんなさい、おくれました。

language_specific.usage: An apology; おくれました means that the speaker was late.

common.sentence: じゃあ、またね。

language_specific.usage: A casual farewell suggesting that you will see the other person again.

common.sentence: はじめまして、さとうです。

language_specific.usage: Said on meeting someone for the first time.

common.sentence: わたしは、さとうです。
common.note: は marks the topic and is pronounced わ; です politely identifies it.

language_specific.usage: A broadly usable first-person pronoun; it is often omitted when understood.

common.sentence: わたしはがくせいです。
あの人は先生です。
common.note: あの人 (あのひと) means that person.

language_specific.usage: Here 先生 identifies someone's occupation.

common.sentence: これはわたしのほんです。
common.note: これは means as for this; の links the book to its owner.

common.sentence: これはかぎですか。
common.note: か at the end makes this a polite question.

language_specific.pronunciation: ぎ has a voiced consonant, unlike き.

common.sentence: それはなんですか。

language_specific.usage: なん is the form of 何 used before です in this question.

common.sentence: これはわたしのかさです。

language_specific.usage: Refers to a thing near the speaker.

common.sentence: それはだれのかばんですか。
common.note: だれの asks whose; かばん means bag.

common.sentence: えきはどこですか。
common.note: えき means station.

common.sentence: ここはとしょかんです。
common.note: としょかん means library.

language_specific.usage: Refers to a place near the speaker.

common.sentence: いえはえきのそばです。
common.note: えきのそば means near the station.

common.sentence: にわにいぬがいます。
common.note: にわに means in the garden; います indicates an animate being is there.

common.sentence: ねこがいすにいます。
common.note: いすにいます means is on the chair.

common.sentence: ははがすきです。
common.note: The speaker says they like their mother.

language_specific.usage: Used for one's own mother when speaking to someone outside the family.

common.sentence: ちちはいま、いえです。
common.note: いま、いえです means is at home now.

language_specific.usage: Used for one's own father when speaking to someone outside the family.

common.sentence: ともだちとえきであいます。
common.note: と marks the person met; えきであいます means meet at the station.

common.sentence: おみずをください。
common.note: をください is a polite way to request something.

language_specific.usage: The prefix お makes みず sound more polite in this request.

common.sentence: あたたかいおちゃです。
common.note: あたたかい means warm.

common.sentence: あさはパンをたべます。
common.note: パン (ぱん) をたべます means eat bread.

common.sentence: ひるにごはんをたべます。
common.note: ひるに means at midday; たべます means eat.

language_specific.usage: ごはん can mean cooked rice or a meal; either interpretation is possible here.

common.sentence: りんごがすきです。
common.note: が marks the thing liked; です makes the statement polite.

language_specific.usage: Expresses a preference; the person who likes something is understood here.

common.sentence: このみかんはあまいです。
common.note: このみかん means this mandarin.

common.sentence: このおちゃはあついです。
common.note: このおちゃ means this tea.

language_specific.usage: Describes the temperature of the tea.

common.sentence: きょうはあめです。
common.note: きょうは means as for today.

language_specific.usage: In this weather statement, あめ means rain.

common.sentence: あしたはやすみです。
common.note: やすみです means it is a day off.

common.sentence: はい、がくせいです。
common.note: がくせいです means someone is a student; the person is understood from context.

language_specific.usage: A polite affirmative response to a question or statement.

common.sentence: いいえ、先生ではありません。
common.note: 先生ではありません means someone is not a teacher; the person is understood from context.

language_specific.usage: A polite negative response to a question or statement.

common.sentence: おちゃをください。
common.note: を marks the item requested.

language_specific.usage: Used after a noun marked by を to make a polite request.

common.sentence: ごはん、いただきます。

language_specific.usage: Conventionally said before starting a meal.

common.sentence: おいしかった。ごちそうさま。
common.note: おいしかった means it was delicious.

language_specific.usage: Conventionally said after a meal; ごちそうさまでした is more polite.

common.sentence: いってきます、またあとで。

language_specific.usage: Said when leaving a place to which one expects to return.

common.sentence: わたしはマンションにすんでいます。
common.note: すんでいます means 'live' in a place.

language_specific.pronunciation: The small ョ combines with シ; ン counts as one mora each time.
language_specific.usage: In Japanese, マンション usually means an apartment building, not a mansion.

common.sentence: コンセントはどこにありますか。

language_specific.pronunciation: Each ン counts as one mora.
language_specific.usage: This means an electrical outlet or socket.

common.sentence: ペットボトルのおみずをください。

language_specific.pronunciation: The small ッ indicates a lengthened consonant in ト; ペ has a handakuten and ボ has a dakuten.
language_specific.usage: This refers to a PET drink bottle. When typing, select the small ッ rather than a full-size ツ.

common.sentence: スーパーでパンをかいます。
common.note: かいます means 'buy'.

language_specific.pronunciation: Both vowels marked by ー are long.
language_specific.usage: スーパー commonly means a supermarket. Include both long-vowel marks when typing.

common.sentence: バスでえきにいきます。
common.note: いきます means 'go'; で marks the means of transport.

language_specific.pronunciation: バ is voiced and written with dakuten.

common.sentence: えきでタクシーにのります。
common.note: にのります means 'get into' a vehicle here.

language_specific.pronunciation: The final シー has a long vowel.

common.sentence: テレビをみますか。
common.note: みます means 'watch' here.

language_specific.pronunciation: The final ビ is voiced; there is no long vowel.

common.sentence: あさ、ラジオをききます。
common.note: ききます means 'listen to' here.

language_specific.pronunciation: ジ and オ form separate morae.

common.sentence: スマホはかばんのなかです。
common.note: なか means 'inside'.

language_specific.usage: スマホ is a common short form of スマートフォン.

common.sentence: パソコンをつかいます。
common.note: つかいます means 'use'.

language_specific.pronunciation: パ has a handakuten; the final ン counts as one mora.
language_specific.usage: パソコン is the usual word for a personal computer.

common.sentence: このアプリはべんりです。
common.note: べんり means 'convenient' or 'useful'.

language_specific.pronunciation: プ has a handakuten.
language_specific.usage: アプリ is a common short form for a software application.

common.sentence: ともだちにメールをおくります。
common.note: おくります means 'send'; に marks the recipient.

language_specific.pronunciation: メー has a long vowel.
language_specific.usage: メール commonly means an email or electronic message.

common.sentence: このページのコピーをください。
common.note: ページ means 'page'.

language_specific.pronunciation: ピー has a long vowel and a handakuten.

common.sentence: カメラでねこをとります。
common.note: とります means 'take a picture' here.

common.sentence: かぎはポケットにあります。

language_specific.pronunciation: The small ッ indicates a lengthened consonant in ト; ポ has a handakuten.
language_specific.usage: When typing, select the small ッ rather than a full-size ツ.

common.sentence: ねこはベッドのうえにいます。
common.note: うえ means 'on top'.

language_specific.pronunciation: The small ッ indicates a lengthened consonant in ド; ベ and ド have dakuten.

common.sentence: ソファにすわります。
common.note: にすわります means 'sit on' here.

language_specific.pronunciation: ファ is one mora, made with フ and a small ァ.
language_specific.usage: When typing, select the small ァ rather than a full-size ア.

common.sentence: しろいシャツをきます。
common.note: しろい means 'white'; きます means 'put on' here.

language_specific.pronunciation: シャ is one mora, made with シ and a small ャ.
language_specific.usage: When typing, select the small ャ rather than a full-size ヤ.

common.sentence: さむいです。コートをきます。
common.note: さむい means 'cold'; きます means 'put on'.

language_specific.pronunciation: コー has a long vowel.

common.sentence: このセーターはあたたかいです。
common.note: あたたかい means 'warm'.

language_specific.pronunciation: Both vowels marked by ー are long.

common.sentence: このジャケットをください。

language_specific.pronunciation: ジャ is one mora; the small ッ indicates a lengthened consonant in ト.
language_specific.usage: When typing, use small ャ and small ッ.

common.sentence: つめたいジュースをください。
common.note: つめたい means 'cold' to the touch or taste.

language_specific.pronunciation: ジ and small ュ combine; ー makes the vowel long.
language_specific.usage: ジュース can also refer broadly to sweet soft drinks, depending on context.

common.sentence: パンにチーズをのせます。
common.note: のせます means 'put on top'.

language_specific.pronunciation: チー has a long vowel; ズ is voiced.

common.sentence: スーパーでパンをえらびます。
common.note: えらびます means 'choose'.

language_specific.pronunciation: パ has a handakuten; ン counts as one mora.
language_specific.usage: パン means bread, not a cooking pan.

common.sentence: ケーキとおちゃをください。

language_specific.pronunciation: ケー has a long vowel.

common.sentence: このチョコはあまいです。

language_specific.pronunciation: チョ is one mora, made with チ and a small ョ.
language_specific.usage: チョコ is a common short form of チョコレート. When typing, select the small ョ.

common.sentence: サンドイッチをたべますか。
common.note: たべます means 'eat'.

language_specific.pronunciation: ン counts as one mora, and the small ッ indicates a lengthened consonant in チ.

common.sentence: あついコーヒーをのみます。
common.note: のみます means 'drink'.

language_specific.pronunciation: Both vowels marked by ー are long.
language_specific.usage: Include both long-vowel marks when typing.

common.sentence: コップにおみずをいれます。
common.note: いれます means 'put in' or 'pour into' here.

language_specific.pronunciation: The small ッ indicates a lengthened consonant in プ, which has a handakuten.
language_specific.usage: コップ commonly means a drinking glass or tumbler.

common.sentence: スプーンをください。

language_specific.pronunciation: プー has a long vowel; the final ン counts as one mora.

common.sentence: ケーキはフォークでたべます。
common.note: で marks the utensil; たべます means 'eat'.

language_specific.pronunciation: フォ uses a small ォ, and its vowel is long.
language_specific.usage: When typing, select the small ォ rather than a full-size オ.

common.sentence: ナイフをください。

language_specific.pronunciation: ナ and イ form separate morae.

common.sentence: レストランはえきのまえです。
common.note: まえ means 'in front'.

language_specific.pronunciation: The final ン counts as one mora.

common.sentence: すみません、トイレはどこですか。

language_specific.usage: トイレ can refer to the restroom as well as the toilet itself.

common.sentence: エレベーターはどこですか。

language_specific.pronunciation: Both vowels marked by ー are long.
language_specific.usage: Include both long-vowel marks when typing.

common.sentence: ドアをしめてください。
common.note: しめてください means 'please close'.

language_specific.pronunciation: ド and ア form separate morae.

common.sentence: おかいけいはカードでいいですか。
common.note: おかいけい means payment or checkout; でいいですか asks whether that payment method is acceptable.

language_specific.pronunciation: カー has a long vowel; ド is voiced.
language_specific.usage: In a payment situation, カード commonly means a credit or debit card.

common.sentence: レジはあちらです。
common.note: あちら means 'over there' politely.

language_specific.usage: レジ refers to the cash register or checkout area.

common.sentence: ホテルはえきのちかくです。
common.note: ちかく means 'near'.

language_specific.pronunciation: Each of ホ, テ, and ル counts as one mora.

common.sentence: えきでチケットをかいます。
common.note: かいます means 'buy'.

language_specific.pronunciation: The small ッ indicates a lengthened consonant in ト.

common.sentence: わたしのおばさんはパンがすきです。

language_specific.pronunciation: お・ば・さ・ん has four morae; the vowel in ば is short, and ん takes one mora.
language_specific.usage: Here the word refers to the speaker's aunt; it can also refer to a middle-aged woman.

common.sentence: わたしのおばあさんはどこですか。

language_specific.pronunciation: お・ば・あ・さ・ん has five morae; あ lengthens the vowel in ば by one mora, and ん takes one mora.
language_specific.usage: Here the word refers to the speaker's grandmother; it can also refer to an elderly woman.

common.sentence: ここになまえをかいてください。
common.note: なまえ means name; かいてください means please write.

language_specific.pronunciation: こ・こ has two morae, each with a short vowel.
language_specific.usage: ここに marks where the name should be written.

common.sentence: いもうとはこうこうのせいとです。
common.note: いもうと means younger sister; せいと means student.

language_specific.pronunciation: こ・う・こ・う has four morae; each う lengthens the preceding o vowel by one mora.

common.sentence: あした、いえにきてください。
common.note: 〜てください is a polite request.

language_specific.pronunciation: き・て has two morae, with no っ between them.
language_specific.usage: This is a request to come to a home.

common.sentence: てがみにきってをはります。
common.note: てがみ means letter; はります means stick on.

language_specific.pronunciation: き・っ・て has three morae; っ takes one mora and holds the following t consonant.

common.sentence: かこのことをはなします。
common.note: はなします means 'talk' here.

language_specific.pronunciation: か・こ has two morae, with a single k sound between the vowels.

common.sentence: なまえをかっこにいれてください。
common.note: なまえ means name; いれてください means please put in.

language_specific.pronunciation: か・っ・こ has three morae; っ takes one mora and holds the following k consonant.
language_specific.usage: Here かっこ means the punctuation marks around the name.

common.sentence: ねつがあります。びょういんへいきます。
common.note: ねつがあります means I have a fever.

language_specific.pronunciation: びょ・う・い・ん has four morae. Small ょ combines with び; う lengthens its vowel, and ん takes one mora.
language_specific.usage: This is a medical facility.

common.sentence: びよういんでかみをきります。
common.note: かみ means hair; きります means cut.

language_specific.pronunciation: び・よ・う・い・ん has five morae. Full-size よ is a separate mora; う lengthens its vowel, and ん takes one mora.
language_specific.usage: This is a place to have one's hair done.

common.sentence: わたしのおじさんがきます。
common.note: きます means 'comes' here.

language_specific.pronunciation: お・じ・さ・ん has four morae; the vowel in じ is short, and ん takes one mora.
language_specific.usage: Here the word refers to the speaker's uncle; it can also refer to a middle-aged man.

common.sentence: わたしのおじいさんにおちゃをください。
common.note: に marks the person receiving the tea.

language_specific.pronunciation: お・じ・い・さ・ん has five morae; い lengthens the vowel in じ by one mora, and ん takes one mora.
language_specific.usage: Here the word refers to the speaker's grandfather; it can also refer to an elderly man.

common.sentence: きょうはゆきです。

language_specific.pronunciation: ゆ・き has two morae; the vowel in ゆ is short.

common.sentence: ゆうきがひつようです。
common.note: ひつようです means is needed.

language_specific.pronunciation: ゆ・う・き has three morae; う lengthens the vowel in ゆ by one mora.

common.sentence: あのきにとりがいます。
common.note: あのき means that tree.

language_specific.pronunciation: と・り has two morae; the vowel in と is short.

common.sentence: このとおりをまっすぐいきます。
common.note: まっすぐ means straight ahead.

language_specific.pronunciation: と・お・り has three morae; お lengthens the vowel in と by one mora.

common.sentence: えきのまえにビルがあります。

language_specific.pronunciation: ビ・ル has two morae; the vowel in ビ is short.

common.sentence: ばんごはんにビールをのみます。

language_specific.pronunciation: ビ・ー・ル has three morae; ー lengthens the vowel in ビ by one mora.

common.sentence: ねつがあります。みずをください。

language_specific.pronunciation: ね・つ has two morae; full-size つ is a syllable, not a small っ.

common.sentence: きのねっこはつちのなかです。
common.note: つち means soil.

language_specific.pronunciation: ね・っ・こ has three morae; small っ takes one mora and holds the following k consonant.

common.sentence: えきのまえにさかがあります。

language_specific.pronunciation: さ・か has two morae, with a single k sound between the vowels.

common.sentence: あねはさっかです。
common.note: あね means my older sister.

language_specific.pronunciation: さ・っ・か has three morae; っ takes one mora and holds the following k consonant.

common.sentence: ここにいてください。
common.note: 〜てください is a polite request.

language_specific.pronunciation: い・て has two morae, with no っ between them.
language_specific.usage: This asks someone to remain here.

common.sentence: さきにえきへいってください。
common.note: さきに means ahead of someone else.

language_specific.pronunciation: い・っ・て has three morae; っ takes one mora and holds the following t consonant.
language_specific.usage: This asks someone to go to the station ahead of others.

common.sentence: このまちにはこうえんがあります。
common.note: こうえん means park.

language_specific.pronunciation: ま・ち has two morae, with no っ before ち.

common.sentence: マッチでろうそくにひをつけます。
common.note: ろうそく means candle; ひをつけます means light it.

language_specific.pronunciation: マ・ッ・チ has three morae; ッ takes one mora and holds the consonant at the start of チ.
language_specific.usage: This is a match used to light a flame.

common.sentence: そとでおとがします。
common.note: おとがします means a sound is heard.

language_specific.pronunciation: お・と has two morae, with a single t sound between the vowels.

common.sentence: おっとはいま、かいしゃにいます。
common.note: かいしゃ means company or workplace.

language_specific.pronunciation: お・っ・と has three morae; っ takes one mora and holds the following t consonant.
language_specific.usage: 夫 is a way to refer to one's own husband.

common.sentence: きょうはともだちとあいます。

language_specific.pronunciation: きょ・う has two morae. Small ょ combines with き; う lengthens the resulting vowel by one mora.

common.sentence: あねはきようです。ふくをつくります。
common.note: あね means my older sister; ふくをつくります means makes clothes.

language_specific.pronunciation: き・よ・う has three morae. Full-size よ is separate from き; う lengthens the vowel in よ by one mora.
language_specific.usage: Here きよう describes someone's manual skill.

common.sentence: がっこうのせんぱいにそうだんします。
common.note: がっこう means school; そうだんします means consult someone.

language_specific.pronunciation: せ・ん・ぱ・い has four morae; ん takes one mora and may sound m-like before p.
language_specific.usage: A 先輩 is someone senior to the speaker in a shared setting.

common.sentence: あさ、こうえんをさんぽします。
common.note: こうえん means park.

language_specific.pronunciation: さ・ん・ぽ has three morae; ん takes one mora and may sound m-like before p.
language_specific.usage: さんぽします means to take a walk.

common.sentence: ちちはあさ、しんぶんをよみます。
common.note: よみます means read.

language_specific.pronunciation: し・ん・ぶ・ん has four morae. Each ん takes one mora; the first may sound m-like before b, while the final one varies with context.

common.sentence: ははにでんわをかけます。

language_specific.pronunciation: で・ん・わ has three morae; ん takes one mora, and its nasal quality varies with the following sound.
language_specific.usage: 電話をかける means to make a phone call.

common.sentence: あしたのてんきはあめです。

language_specific.pronunciation: て・ん・き has three morae; ん takes one mora and may sound like the nasal in English 'sing' before k.

common.sentence: あさごはんにりんごをたべます。

language_specific.pronunciation: り・ん・ご has three morae; ん takes one mora and may sound like the nasal in English 'sing' before g.

common.sentence: としょかんでほんをかります。
common.note: かります means borrow.

language_specific.pronunciation: ほ・ん has two morae; ん takes one mora, and its sound varies with the following context.

common.sentence: きんようびにびょういんへいきます。

language_specific.pronunciation: き・ん・よ・う・び has five morae. ん takes one mora and varies before y; full-size よ is separate, and う lengthens its vowel.

common.sentence: かばんにかぎをいれます。
common.note: かぎ means key.

language_specific.pronunciation: か・ば・ん has three morae; ん takes one mora, and its sound varies with the following context.

common.sentence: このほんはせんえんです。

language_specific.pronunciation: せ・ん・え・ん has four morae; each ん takes one mora, and its nasal quality varies with context.

common.sentence: もういちどおねがいします。
common.cloze: もういちどおねがいします
common.answer: もういちどおねがいします
common.lemma: もういちどおねがいします

language_specific.target_reading: もういちどおねがいします
language_specific.usage: Use this to ask someone to repeat what they said.

common.sentence: ゆっくりはなしてください。
common.note: はなしてください means “please speak.”

common.sentence: 「あした」はどういういみですか。
すみません、よくわかりません。

language_specific.usage: A polite way to say that an explanation or statement is unclear.

common.sentence: ここまで、わかりますか。
common.note: ここまで means “up to this point.”

common.sentence: 「はし」ですよね。

language_specific.usage: Here the speaker checks whether the word is はし.

common.sentence: あなたのなまえのつづりをかいてください。
common.note: なまえ means “name,” and つづり means “spelling.”

language_specific.usage: With ください, this asks the listener to write down the spelling of their name.

common.sentence: 「water」はにほんごでなんですか。

language_specific.usage: The question asks for the Japanese word for “water.”

common.sentence: えいごでおねがいします。

language_specific.usage: This asks the other person to speak or explain in English.

common.sentence: あしたですね。わかりました。

language_specific.usage: This acknowledges that the speaker has understood the information.

common.sentence: ここにすわってもいいですか。
common.note: すわって is the te-form of すわる, “sit.” The permission component もいいですか follows it.

language_specific.usage: After すわって, もいいですか asks permission to sit here.

common.sentence: このいす、いいですか。
common.note: いす means “chair.”

language_specific.usage: In this context, the speaker asks whether the chair is available to use.

common.sentence: ドアをあけてください。

language_specific.usage: With ください, this is a polite request to open the door.

common.sentence: ちょっとてつだってください。
common.note: ちょっと softens the request here.

language_specific.usage: With ください, this asks someone for a little help.

common.sentence: コーヒーをおねがいします。

language_specific.usage: This politely orders coffee.

common.sentence: メニューをみせてください。

language_specific.usage: With ください, this asks someone to show the speaker the menu.

common.sentence: おかいけい、おねがいします。

language_specific.usage: Use this at a restaurant or shop to ask to pay.

common.sentence: かぎがみつからないんです。
common.note: かぎ means “key.” Learn this missing-object expression as a chunk.

language_specific.usage: The speaker explains that they cannot find the key.

common.sentence: かさをさがしてください。
common.note: かさ means “umbrella.”

language_specific.usage: With ください, this asks someone to look for the umbrella.

common.sentence: にもつをもってください。
common.note: にもつ means “luggage” or “belongings.”

language_specific.usage: With ください, this asks someone to hold or carry the belongings.

common.sentence: なにがすきですか。

language_specific.usage: With なに and the final か, this asks what the other person likes.

common.sentence: コーヒーはにがてです。

language_specific.usage: This is a mild way to say that coffee is not to the speaker's taste.

common.sentence: おちゃとコーヒー、どちらがいいですか。

language_specific.usage: This politely asks for a choice between the two drinks.

common.sentence: コーヒーよりおちゃのほうがいいです。

language_specific.usage: With より and いいです, this expresses a preference for tea over coffee.

common.sentence: おみずがほしいです。

language_specific.usage: The speaker says they want water.

common.sentence: おちゃをのみませんか。

language_specific.usage: This is an invitation to have tea together, despite its negative form.

common.sentence: いっしょにいきましょう。
common.note: いきましょう means “let's go.”

common.sentence: わたしはこれにします。

language_specific.usage: This announces the speaker's choice from the available options.

common.sentence: おちゃをもういっぱい、いかがですか。
common.note: もういっぱい means “one more cup” here.

language_specific.usage: This is a polite offer of another cup of tea.

common.sentence: おちゃはあまりすきじゃないです。

language_specific.usage: With the negative すきじゃないです, this softens the dislike.

common.sentence: あしたはあめだとおもいます。

language_specific.usage: This presents tomorrow's rain as the speaker's expectation.

common.sentence: 「あしたですね」「そうです」

language_specific.usage: The reply confirms that tomorrow is correct.

common.sentence: 「これですか」「ちがいます」

language_specific.usage: The reply says that the indicated item is not the right one.

common.sentence: あしたはどうですか。あしたはちょっとむずかしいです。

language_specific.usage: Here ちょっと softens the response that tomorrow is difficult.

common.sentence: あしたはたぶんあめです。

language_specific.usage: This marks the statement as uncertain.

common.sentence: じかんはまだわかりません。
common.note: じかん means “time.”

language_specific.usage: With わかりません, this says the time is not known yet.

common.sentence: すみません、まちがえました。
きょうです。あ、ちがいます、あしたです。

language_specific.usage: The speaker corrects their statement that it is today, then says it is tomorrow.

common.sentence: なんじにしまりますか。
common.note: しまりますか means “does it close?” Learn the question as a practical chunk.

language_specific.usage: This asks for the closing time.

common.sentence: しはらいはカードでもいいですか。
common.note: しはらい means “payment.”

language_specific.usage: This checks whether paying by card is acceptable.

common.sentence: あめです。かさはありますか。
common.note: かさ means umbrella.

language_specific.pronunciation: In the Tokyo word model, あ is high and the pitch falls before め.

common.sentence: このあめはあまいです。
common.note: あまい means sweet.

language_specific.pronunciation: In the Tokyo word model, あめ has no lexical fall; め remains high into a following particle.

common.sentence: ごはんをたべます。はしをください。

language_specific.pronunciation: In the Tokyo word model, は is high and the pitch falls before し; the following を is also low.
language_specific.usage: The speaker asks for chopsticks to eat a meal.

common.sentence: かわにはしがあります。

language_specific.pronunciation: In the Tokyo word model, は is low and し is high; the fall after し can be heard on the following が.
language_specific.usage: The sentence says there is a bridge over the river.

common.sentence: ゆきはすきですが、あめはいやです。
common.note: The sentence contrasts liking snow with disliking rain.

language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: To highlight the contrast with ゆきは, you can give あめ in あめは extra prominence. Rain あめ has a Tokyo lexical fall after あ; sentence intonation varies with context.
language_specific.usage: The two は-marked topics contrast snow, which the speaker likes, with rain, which the speaker dislikes.

common.sentence: ケーキですか。いいえ、あめです。

language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: Give あめ informative focus when correcting the guess. Its Tokyo word model has no lexical fall; focus does not add a lexical fall.
language_specific.usage: The reply corrects a guess of cake: it is candy.

common.sentence: はしでたべますか。

language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: A rise at the end can mark the question. The Tokyo word model for chopsticks still falls after は; the question rise does not move that lexical fall to the later bridge pattern.
language_specific.usage: The question asks whether someone eats with chopsticks.

common.sentence: はしでかわをわたります。
common.note: かわ means river; わたります means cross.

language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: You can group はしで as the means of crossing, with a light boundary before かわをわたります. That boundary is optional and depends on the intended phrasing.
language_specific.usage: The sentence describes crossing the river by bridge.

common.sentence: ねこがすきです。

language_specific.pronunciation: The う vowel in す may devoice between the voiceless sounds s and k. Keep す in the spelling.

common.sentence: くつはここです。

language_specific.pronunciation: The う vowel in く may devoice between the voiceless sounds k and ts. It remains in the spelling.

common.sentence: かばんはつくえのしたです。
common.note: つくえ means desk.

language_specific.pronunciation: The い vowel in し may devoice between the voiceless sounds sh and t; it is still written.

common.sentence: きたはどちらですか。
common.note: どちら means which direction.

language_specific.pronunciation: The い vowel in き may devoice between k and t. Do not omit き from the spelling.

common.sentence: あのひとはだれですか。

language_specific.pronunciation: The い vowel in ひ may devoice between the voiceless sounds h and t; it remains part of the written word.

common.sentence: このふくはあおいです。
common.note: あおい means blue.

language_specific.pronunciation: The う vowel in ふ may devoice between the voiceless sounds f and k. Keep the ordinary spelling.

common.sentence: これはおちゃです。
common.note: おちゃ means tea.

language_specific.pronunciation: At the end of a phrase, the う vowel in す may be devoiced. The spelling remains です.

common.sentence: みずをのみます。

language_specific.pronunciation: At the end of a phrase, the う vowel in す may be devoiced. Keep ます in the spelling.

common.sentence: そっち？いいえ、こっちです。

language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: Give こっち the focus when correcting the proposed direction; a short pause after いいえ helps separate the correction.
language_specific.usage: Casual speech; そっち refers to the other person's side or direction.

common.sentence: だれですか。わたしです。

language_specific.pronunciation: In the answer, make わたし the informative focus: it supplies the person asked for.

common.sentence: どれですか。これです。

language_specific.pronunciation: Focus これ in the reply to identify the item among the available choices.
language_specific.usage: どれ asks which one.

common.sentence: でんわのひとはだれですか。
common.note: でんわ means telephone.

language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: A light boundary after でんわのひとは can set up the topic; give だれ informative focus to ask for the identity of the person on the phone.
language_specific.usage: The speaker asks who the person on the phone is.

common.sentence: これは、なんですか。

language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: After a light boundary following これは, focus なん when asking what the item is.
language_specific.usage: なん is the form used before です.

common.sentence: トイレは、どこですか。

language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: A light boundary after トイレは introduces the topic; focus どこ to ask for its location.

common.sentence: あしたですか。そうです。

language_specific.pronunciation: In the reply, focus そう to confirm the proposed day; keep its long vowel for two morae.
language_specific.usage: あした means tomorrow.

common.sentence: おちゃ、いりますか。はい。
common.note: いりますか asks whether someone wants or needs something.

language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: Say はい as a separate response after the question, with a clear boundary between the two turns.
language_specific.usage: The reply accepts the offer of tea.

common.sentence: あしたです。そうですか。

language_specific.pronunciation: A gentle, relatively level or falling ending can acknowledge the information; a rise can instead sound like a request for confirmation.
language_specific.usage: The first speaker says it is tomorrow.

common.sentence: これ、ただです。ほんとう？
common.note: ただ means free of charge.

language_specific.pronunciation: A rising ending can convey surprise and a request for confirmation. The final う extends the vowel.
language_specific.usage: This bare question is casual.

common.sentence: このほんをよんでもいいですか。
common.note: このほんをよんでも sets up the request to read this book.

language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: A gentle rise at the end can mark this as a request for permission.
language_specific.usage: The full sentence asks permission to read this book.

common.sentence: 「あしたです。」「すみません、もういちど。」
common.note: あした means tomorrow.

language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: Use a gentle request intonation in the second turn; a small boundary after すみません is optional. もう has a long vowel.
language_specific.usage: The second speaker asks the first to repeat what they said.

common.sentence: おちゃ、いりますか。ええ。

language_specific.pronunciation: A settled, falling response can signal agreement; hold the vowel for two morae.
language_specific.usage: Here ええ accepts the offer of tea.

common.sentence: おちゃですか。いいえ、みずです。

language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: A gentle falling response followed by a small pause prepares the correction みずです.
language_specific.usage: The speaker corrects the guess: it is water.

common.sentence: あした、だいじょうぶですか。

language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: A gentle rise at the end of the full question can invite confirmation. In だいじょうぶ, keep じょう long.
language_specific.usage: This checks whether tomorrow works for the listener.

common.sentence: おちゃです。どうぞ。

language_specific.pronunciation: A gentle falling ending can make the offer sound settled; どう has a long vowel.
language_specific.usage: The speaker offers tea to someone.

common.sentence: あかがすきです。

language_specific.pronunciation: あか has two morae, both with the vowel /a/. In romaji input, aka gives あか.

common.sentence: いかはすきですか。

language_specific.pronunciation: いか has two morae, with /i/ followed by /a/. In romaji input, ika gives いか.

common.sentence: うみはどこですか。

language_specific.pronunciation: うみ has two morae, with /u/ followed by /i/. In romaji input, umi gives うみ.

common.sentence: このえはすてきです。
common.note: すてき means lovely.

language_specific.pronunciation: え is one mora with the vowel /e/. In romaji input, e gives え.

common.sentence: このおとはなんですか。

language_specific.pronunciation: おと has two morae, both with the vowel /o/. In romaji input, oto gives おと.

common.sentence: きゅうりをください。

language_specific.pronunciation: きゅうり has three morae: きゅ, う, り. The small ゅ joins き; in romaji input, kyuuri gives きゅうり.

common.sentence: びょうきです。くすりはありますか。
common.note: くすり means medicine.

language_specific.pronunciation: びょうき has three morae: びょ, う, き. The small ょ joins び; in romaji input, byouki gives びょうき.
language_specific.usage: びょうきです means the speaker is ill here.

common.sentence: ゆうびんのまどぐちはここですか。
common.note: まどぐち means counter.

language_specific.pronunciation: ゆうびん has four morae: ゆ, う, び, ん. The second unit of the long vowel and the final ん each count as one mora; in romaji input, yuubin gives ゆうびん.
language_specific.usage: The speaker asks whether this is the postal counter.
